nodes.summary: No task can lower its cost by moving alone: for every task `i` and every other machine `k`, the load of `i`'s machine is at most the load `ℓₖ + wᵢ` that `i` would experience on `k` (Vöcking, *Algorithmic Game Theory*, Proposition 20.2, specialised to identical machines).
nodes.title: Pure Nash equilibrium of the load balancing game

nodes.summary: The makespan is the maximum of the machine loads, so it bounds each of them.
nodes.title: Every load is at most the makespan

nodes.summary: With nonnegative weights every machine load is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Loads are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Under the assignment `A` of tasks of weights `w` to the machines `Fin m`, the load of machine `j` is the total weight `∑_{A(i) = j} wᵢ` of the tasks placed on it (identical machines of speed `1`; Vöcking, *Algorithmic Game Theory*, Chapter 20, Section 20.1).
nodes.title: Load of a machine

nodes.summary: For `m ≥ 1` identical machines and nonnegative weights, every pure Nash equilibrium `A` has `makespan(A) ≤ (2 - 2/(m + 1)) · makespan(B)` for every assignment `B`, in particular for an optimal one.
nodes.title: Price of anarchy for pure equilibria on identical machines

nodes.summary: The social cost of an assignment: the maximum load over the (at least one) machines (Vöcking, *Algorithmic Game Theory*, Chapter 20, Section 20.1.1).
nodes.title: Makespan

nodes.summary: Let `m ≥ 1` identical machines and nonnegative task weights `w` be given. If `A` is a pure Nash equilibrium and `B` is any assignment, then `(m + 1) · makespan(A) ≤ 2m · makespan(B)`.
nodes.title: Price of anarchy for pure equilibria on identical machines (multiplicative form)
Loads add up to the total weight

nodes.summary: Every assignment has makespan at least the average load: `∑ᵢ wᵢ ≤ m · makespan(B)` (the lower bound on the optimum used in the proof of Vöcking, *Algorithmic Game Theory*, Theorem 20.5).
nodes.title: Average load bound

nodes.summary: For nonnegative weights, `wᵢ ≤ makespan(B)` for every task `i` and assignment `B`.
nodes.title: A single task bounds every makespan

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
